paras: The attempted lynching of the Moon brothers was a failed effort by a mob to seize and lynch two or more prisoners held in the jail at Gadsden, Alabama, in March 1882. The mob could not cross the river to reach the jail, and the authorities then moved the prisoners to Birmingham under military guard.

The brothers were held at Gadsden on what the headline over the only surviving report, 'The Moon Murderers', implies was a murder charge. The dispatch gives neither their first names nor their race, and it does not describe the crime or name its victim.

According to a Montgomery dispatch dated Friday, March 24, the mob made 'another demonstration Friday night, with a design to lynch the Moon brothers,' a wording that implies at least one earlier attempt. The dispatch does not make clear whether that Friday was March 24 itself or the week before. Unable to cross the river to the jail, the men withdrew 'after giving notification of their determination to accomplish their purpose.' Strangers had also been seen about the jail at night, 'as if reconnoitering the premises.'

The prisoners were sent to Birmingham, 'where they will be guarded by the military,' and Governor Cobb went up to that part of the state. No report of the brothers' trial or of what became of them appears in the coverage.

The episode survives in a single wire item from Montgomery, printed without comment by the Memphis Daily Appeal on March 25, 1882. Its headline identified the prisoners by the crime alleged against them, and its text treated the mob's threat and the state's response as routine news, without naming anyone in the mob or describing its size.
